$description: Modal dialog for a focused decision or task, with accessible title, scrim and correctly managed modal focus.
name: Dialog

behavior.modality: Block interaction with underlying content while open; show the existing semantic backdrop.
behavior.focus: Move initial focus to a deliberate interactive control; contain tab navigation while modal; restore focus to triggering control after close.
behavior.dismiss: Escape/cancel when appropriate; exceptional non-dismissible flows must explicitly document alternate safe completion.
behavior.actions: Actions use the Button specification; potentially destructive completion must be distinguishable and confirmed where consequences are hard to reverse.
behavior.size: Content-driven within usable viewport and safe areas; never clip enlarged text or create routine horizontal scroll.
behavior.elevation: Level 2 is optional and used only if surface and border do not already distinguish the dialog.

accessibility: Expose a modal dialog role and accessible title, with descriptive content as appropriate.
Keep focus within the modal until dismissal and restore prior focus afterward.
Backdrop is a scrim, not a shadow; do not rely on a shadow alone to communicate modality.
Respect platform screen readers, system back navigation, safe areas, and large text.

web: Use semantic HTML controls, keyboard focus-visible, and 24×24 CSS px minimum targets; prefer more space for touch.
Retain browser zoom and allow labels to wrap or controls to grow.
Prefer native <dialog> showModal(), with aria-labelledby and focus restoration; verify browser focus behavior.
ios: Respect 44pt minimum interactive hit area and Dynamic Type; prefer native Button/Control semantics.
Use native enabled/disabled and accessibility label/state APIs.
android: Respect 48dp minimum interactive target and nonlinear font scaling; prefer native Compose/View control semantics.
Use native enabled/disabled and accessibility semantics.
